title: The Fight
novel:
Ted and Barney [[decided|decide]] to get into a [[physical|physical]] fight to impress two women at the bar. They had never been in a fight before, and they were secretly [[terrified|terrify]].

"I've never [[thrown|throw]] a punch in my life," Barney [[admitted|admit]].

"Me neither," Ted said. But they [[pretended|pretend]] to be tough.

They [[confronted|confront]] a rude regular named Doug at MacLaren's. Doug was short, [[aggressive|aggressive]], and always looking for trouble. The [[confrontation|confrontation]] was [[brief|brief]] — Doug [[shoved|shove]] them both to the floor in seconds.

Ted and Barney [[exaggerated|exaggerate]] the story to the women. "You should have seen us," Barney said. "We were like [[gladiators|gladiator]]."

Meanwhile, Marshall and Lily had a fight about Marshall's [[habit|habit]] of [[overspending|overspend]]. Their argument was [[misinterpreted|misinterpret]] by everyone at the bar. People thought they were breaking up.

"We're fine!" Lily [[insisted|insist]]. "We just fight differently."

The next day, Ted and Barney [[discovered|discover]] that Doug had actually [[punched|punch]] them both while they were [[unconscious|unconscious]]. They had not fought at all — they had been [[knocked|knock]] out instantly.

Everyone at the bar [[hated|hate]] Doug for his [[arrogance|arrogance]]. Ted and Barney felt [[humiliated|humiliate]].

"We're [[cowards|coward]]," Barney said.

"Yes," Ted agreed. "But at least we're honest cowards."

physical.en: related to the body, not the mind

throw.en: to send something through the air

admit.en: to agree that something is true

pretend.en: to act as if something is true when it is not

confront.en: to face someone in a hostile way

exaggerate.en: to make something seem bigger than it is

overspend.en: to spend more money than you should

insist.en: to say firmly that something is true

punch.en: to hit someone with your closed hand

knock.en: to hit someone so they fall

arrogance.en: thinking you are better than others
